en.title: Maximum Sum with Non-Overlapping Adjacent Concatenations
en.description:
Two originally adjacent elements may be concatenated in decimal, but each original element can be used at most once, and a concatenated result cannot be concatenated again. Find the maximum possible sum of the final elements.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol; ranges not given by the source are stated explicitly.
en.input: The first line contains N (1..10000), and the second line contains N integers in 0..200. 0 also takes up one digit, and concatenating 02 gives the value 2.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: 22+35+40=97. Example 2: keep 3 and form 19191 and 913, for a total of 20107. Example 3: 01 can be formed, but its value is still 1, so the maximum sum is 1.
hints: Prefix DP: either keep the last element on its own, or concatenate the last two original elements into one item; take the larger of the two sums.
